validity.recommendation: treat P3381 and P3382 as one pipeline in two stages of rebuild; merge or re-scope so the DN 700 and DN 500 stretches do not both claim the same corridor
validity.researcher_notes: The pipeline is real. The 2021 notice from the gas system operator describes one Shebelinka to Sloviansk line, in service since 1968, 67 km from km 1.1 to km 68.0, being rebuilt in five sections from DN 700 to DN 500. Four sections were already rebuilt before 2021 and a fifth, 13.5 km, was planned. So P3381 (700 mm, 70 km) and P3382 (500 mm, 54 km) very likely describe the same physical corridor before and after rebuild. No source describes two parallel lines. The sheet's two rows share one route file that does not follow the named corridor, so it cannot help decide. Not touching lengths until a person rules on the merge. Wikipedia and the operator notices both give 67 km for the rebuild span.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: The newest dated evidence is the 2021 operator notice: the line works as a reverse dead-end supply line (about 1 million cubic meters a day). I found no source from 2024 or later saying whether the Ukrainian section is in use. The line runs through the Barvinkove, Izium and Sloviansk area near the front, and gas infrastructure in Kramatorsk was hit in 2025, but no source ties damage to this line. Row stays operating; no change proposed because absence of news is not evidence.

summary: "Shebelinka-Slovyansk real; P3381 and P3382 look like one corridor before and after DN700 to DN500 rebuild (duplicate concern); capacity unresolved"
